title: Consensus anchor corpus: embedding accuracy harness, offline scoring, and drift sentinel
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Goal: Build a repeatable, extensible evaluation harness for embedding accuracy that (1) uses a curated consensus anchor corpus across domains, (2) computes stable offline metrics for reranking/semantic search (MRR, nDCG@k, recall@k, pairwise AUC), and (3) provides drift detection and triage playbooks. This ticket covers corpus construction, metric definitions and thresholds, nightly batch runner implementation, telemetry exports, and an alerting path when quality regressions or drift are detected.
acceptance_criteria: A curated consensus anchor corpus (~20k items) with domain tags and difficulty buckets is available in S3 and has a manifest file.
An Airflow DAG (embed_eval_consensus) runs nightly producing a snapshot of offline metrics for each target model variant and dataset slice.
Dashboards in Grafana show historical MRR, nDCG@5, recall@10, cosine-distribution shift and a drift score; alerts trigger when drift score exceeds configured thresholds.
Automated synthetic perturbations (typos, truncation, adversarial synonyms) are included in the harness and metrics are computed on these perturbations.
On-call runbook and triage checklist are documented in Confluence and linked from alerts.
tasks: Design consensus anchor selection criteria and sampling algorithm (stratified by domain, doc length, and difficulty).
Implement corpus builder job (Python) and manifest generation; store artifacts in s3://redwood-embed-eval/consensus/2025-01.
Define metric suite and implement scorer module (MRR, nDCG@k, recall@k, pairwise AUC, embedding drift score).
Add synthetic perturbation pipeline and include automatic per-perturbation metrics.
Build Airflow DAG to run nightly evaluations across model variants; produce CSV/JSON exports and Prometheus metrics.
Create Grafana dashboards and alert rules; wire alerts to pagerduty channel 'embeddings-quality'.
Write runbook for triage and rollback recommendations; include sample PR templates for model rollbacks.
updates: 2025-01-10: Ticket created. Kickoff meeting scheduled with PM, Research, and Platform Observability. Decided to avoid single 'golden' set; instead use 'consensus anchor corpus' composed from customer queries + curated public data + expert annotations.

2025-01-13: Prototype sampling script ready. Using reservoir sampling with stratification by domain and length. Initial corpus target size: 20k, with ~60% synthetic/curated and 40% redwood-customer-anonymized examples.

2025-01-17: Metric definitions reviewed with Research. Agreed to compute MRR@10, nDCG@5, recall@10, pairwise AUC, and a cosine-distribution KL-based drift score. Decided to include per-slice metrics (domain, query length, model temperature).

2025-01-20: Implemented scorer prototype and ran smoke tests against embed-testbench models. Early results: MRR correlates with manual quality checks but shows sensitivity to embedding normalization. Action: normalize embeddings before distance computations in scorer.

2025-01-25: Airflow DAG scaffolded in infra repo (github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pulls/2345). Added job to emit Prometheus metrics via metrics-adapter. Next: finalize alert thresholds with SRE and onboard PagerDuty channel.

2025-01-28: Added perturbation generator (typo, stopword drop, paraphrase via back-translation) and integrated perturbation metrics into nightly reports. Planning a canary run for two weeks before flipping on strict alerts.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Customer data may leak if examples are not properly anonymized. Mitigation: only include hashed IDs and strip PII using the pii-scrubber lambda; run sample audit before publish.
Risk: Nightly job could add load to hosted inference. Mitigation: use dedicated low-priority routing and rate-limit; run evaluations against cached embeddings where possible.
Risk: Metric drift false positives due to platform changes. Mitigation: maintain baseline windows and require sustained drift over 3 consecutive runs before firing high-priority alerts.
next_steps: Finalize corpus manifest format, complete end-to-end nightly run and verify outputs for three model variants, run canary for two weeks, then enable alerts. Assign follow-ups to ENG-62205 (dashboard polish) and ENG-62206 (triage runbook).
